name: Juggle three balls
blurb: The three-ball cascade is the classic “I taught myself something” skill. It is learned in three separate stages, and the only real mistake is trying to do all three at once.
gear: Three beanbags or juggling balls — never bouncy balls
A wall to stand facing, or a bed to catch drops
steps: One ball: throw from hand to hand in an arc peaking at eye height, and let it land in the other hand without reaching. Do 50 clean passes.
Two balls: throw the right ball, and when it reaches its peak throw the left underneath it. Two throws, two catches, stop. Do it from both starting hands, 50 times each.
Three balls with two in one hand: throw one, throw two at the peak, throw three at the peak of two, and let them all drop. You are training the timing, not the catching.
Now catch them. Expect a fortnight of five-catch runs before it suddenly becomes continuous.
Practise facing a wall so your throws stay in a flat plane instead of drifting forwards.
Once the cascade is stable, count runs of 100 and work on keeping your hands low and relaxed.
tips: Throwing forwards is the universal beginner fault. If you are walking across the room, face a wall.
Every throw should be a throw, not a hand-off. Two throws in a row from the same hand means you rushed.
Ten focused minutes daily beats an hour on Sunday. This is a sleep-consolidated skill.
proof: Fifty consecutive catches, standing still, without a drop.
